target.name: EGFR Transactivation by Gastrin
target.description: Gastrin is a gut hormone that drives growth and acid secretion in the stomach, and one way it produces growth signals is by borrowing the epidermal growth factor receptor rather than signalling through its own receptor alone. This transactivation route links a G protein-coupled, Gq-type receptor to the classic receptor tyrosine kinase pathway, and its persistent activation is part of why hypergastrinaemia promotes gastric mucosal hyperplasia and contributes to gastric and colorectal tumour growth.

target.name: netrin-activated signaling pathway
target.description: Netrin-activated signalling tells a growing axon or migrating cell which way to go. Netrins are secreted guidance cues that attract some growth cones and repel others, and the response depends on which receptor is displayed: DCC-family receptors such as DSCAM support attraction, while the UNC5 receptors (UNC5A-D) mediate repulsion and turning away from the netrin source.

target.name: RHOQ GTPase cycle
target.description: RHOQ (TC10), a CDC42-subfamily Rho GTPase, cycles between GDP- and GTP-bound states on exocytic vesicles and recycling endosomes, and its activity is needed for vesicles to fuse with the plasma membrane. This makes the RHOQ GTPase cycle the switch that couples membrane delivery to stimulus: in adipocytes it acts downstream of insulin to permit glucose transporter-containing vesicles to reach the cell surface, so glucose uptake depends on it, and it has also been linked to membrane addition during axon outgrowth.
